text: Which planet is the hottest in our solar system?
explain: Venus is the hottest planet, about 872 degrees Fahrenheit at the surface.

text: Which planet has the shortest day in the solar system?
explain: A day on Jupiter lasts only about 9.9 hours.

text: Which planet spins nearly sideways as it orbits the Sun?
explain: Uranus spins at about a 90-degree angle to its orbit.

text: How long is one year on Uranus?
explain: One year on Uranus is about 84 Earth years.

text: Which planet was first found by mathematics, not by looking?
explain: Neptune was the first planet found through mathematical predictions.

text: The Sun is about how many times wider than Earth?
explain: The Sun is about 100 times wider than Earth.

text: In which year was the Hubble Space Telescope launched?
explain: Hubble was launched on April 24, 1990.

text: About how far from Earth is the Webb telescope as it orbits the Sun?
explain: Webb orbits the Sun about 1.5 million kilometers from Earth.

text: How many layers does Webb's sunshield have?
explain: Webb has a 5-layer sunshield that blocks infrared light from the Sun.

text: Who discovered Saturn's moon Titan in 1655?
explain: Christiaan Huygens discovered Titan on March 25, 1655.

text: Which spacecraft first explored Pluto up close?
explain: New Horizons was the first spacecraft to explore Pluto up close, on July 14, 2015.

text: Which spacecraft has visited both Uranus and Neptune?
explain: Voyager 2 is the only spacecraft to visit Uranus and Neptune.
check: only spacecraft to visit Uranus and Neptune

text: The Ingenuity helicopter was built for five flights. How many did it fly?
explain: Ingenuity completed 72 flights on Mars over nearly three years.

text: When did Voyager 1 cross into interstellar space?
explain: Voyager 1 crossed into interstellar space in August 2012.

text: About how long does the space station take to circle Earth?
explain: The International Space Station circles Earth about every 90 minutes.

text: How many sunrises and sunsets does the station crew see each day?
explain: The crew sees 16 sunrises and sunsets every day.

text: Since when has the space station always had people aboard?
explain: The space station has been continuously occupied since November 2000.

text: How long does the Moon take to orbit Earth?
explain: The Moon takes about 27.3 days to orbit Earth.

text: On average, how far away is the Moon?
explain: The Moon is on average 238,855 miles from Earth.

text: In which year did a spacecraft first show us the Moon's far side?
explain: A Soviet spacecraft flew past the Moon's far side in 1959.

text: How much Moon rock and soil did Apollo astronauts bring home?
explain: Apollo astronauts brought back 842 pounds of lunar rocks and soil.

text: How long is the cycle of rising and falling sunspot numbers?
explain: Sunspot numbers follow a natural 11-year cycle.

text: How long does sunlight take to reach Mars?
explain: Sunlight needs about 13 minutes to reach Mars.

text: How far is Earth's axis tilted from its orbit plane?
explain: Earth's axis is tilted 23.4 degrees, which gives us seasons.

text: How much of Earth's water is in the oceans?
explain: About 96.5 percent of Earth's water is in the global oceans.
check: about 96.5%, being in the global oceans

text: How long is one year on Mercury?
explain: Mercury circles the Sun every 88 Earth days.

text: How long does Saturn take to orbit the Sun once?
explain: Saturn takes about 29.4 Earth years to orbit the Sun.

text: If Jupiter were hollow, how many Earths could fit inside?
explain: If Jupiter were a hollow shell, 1,000 Earths could fit inside it.

text: Saturn's rings are very wide. How thick are they, typically?
explain: Saturn's main rings are typically only about 30 feet thick.

text: How long was Neptune's first orbit since it was discovered?
explain: Neptune finished its first 165-year orbit since discovery in 2011.

text: In 2006, Pluto was reclassified as what?
explain: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
check: reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006

text: Which dwarf planet was the first to get a spacecraft visit?
explain: Ceres was the first dwarf planet to receive a visit from a spacecraft.
check: first dwarf planet to receive a visit

text: Vesta is the largest asteroid. About how wide is it?
explain: Vesta is about 329 miles across.

text: The Perseid meteors are pieces of which comet?
explain: The Perseids come from comet Swift-Tuttle.
check: comet swift-tuttle, which swings by the sun

text: How long does the solar system take to circle the galaxy's center?
explain: The solar system takes about 230 million years to make one trip.

text: About how old is the Sun?
explain: The Sun formed about 4.6 billion years ago from gas and dust.

text: About how far away is the nearest known black hole?
explain: The nearest known black hole, Gaia BH1, is about 1,500 light-years away.

text: What sits at the center of our Milky Way galaxy?
explain: Stars orbiting near the center show a supermassive black hole sits there.

text: Which NASA probe flies closest to the Sun?
explain: Parker Solar Probe will come within about 3.9 million miles of the Sun.

text: Which spacecraft made Saturn its home for 13 years?
explain: Cassini spent 13 years at Saturn.

text: What is the Perseverance rover looking for on Mars?
explain: Perseverance looks for signs of ancient microbial life on Mars.

text: Which asteroid moonlet did the DART spacecraft hit in 2022?
explain: DART hit Dimorphos, a small moonlet that orbits a larger asteroid.

text: From which asteroid did OSIRIS-REx collect rocks and dust?
explain: OSIRIS-REx collected rocks and dust from asteroid Bennu.
check: sample of rocks and dust from bennu

text: In which year did Apollo 11 launch?
explain: Apollo 11 launched on July 16, 1969.

text: What does the TESS space telescope search for?
explain: TESS searches for exoplanets, planets around other stars.
check: tess discovers exoplanets, worlds beyond our solar system

text: About how many satellites make up the GPS system?
explain: GPS is a system of more than 30 navigation satellites.
